title: Shortest Path to Get Food
summary: You start at the '*' cell in an m x n grid and need to find the shortest path to reach any '#' cell.
statement: You start at the '*' cell in an m x n grid and need to find the shortest path to reach any '#' cell. The grid contains free space ('O'), obstacles ('X'), and your starting position. You can move to adjacent cells (north, east, south, west) if they are not obstructed by 'X'. If no path to a food cell exists, return -1.
constraints: Grid characters are * for the single start, # for food, O for open cells, and X for blocked cells.
Move four-directionally and return the fewest steps to any food cell, or -1 if unreachable.
hints: All moves have equal cost, so breadth-first search discovers cells in nondecreasing distance.
Start a queue at * and expand unseen, nonblocked four-neighbors.
Return distance+1 when a neighbor is #; enqueue O cells; return -1 if the queue empties.
The first discovered food has the minimum possible number of edges by the BFS layer invariant.
editorial: The first discovered food has the minimum possible number of edges by the BFS layer invariant.
